3. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that the suit land situated at Mouja Chandkati under police station Jhalakati being CS khatian No. 30 (Karsha right) bearing CS plot No. 201, 202 measuring an area 1.83 acres of land except tenanted land belonged to Abdur Gafur as 6 anna share, Amina Begum as 2 anna share, Hinguluddin as 2 anna 10 gonda share, Alip Khalifa as 4 anna  share, Maherjan Bibi as 15 gonda share and Arobjan Bibi as 15 gonda share and accordingly CS khatian was recorded. It is further stated that Abdur Gafur died without any issue, leaving his wife and sister: Amina Begum; that thus Amina Begum got 8 anna share and later on Amina Begum died without any issue, leaving two cousins Hinguluddin and Alif Khalifa; that Alif Khalifa got 8 anna share and then Alif Khalifa died, leaving one son Meseruddin Khalifa and one daughter Mayajan; that Meseruddin got 5 anna 6 gonda 2 Kara and 2 kranti share measuring an area of 61 decimals of land; that Mayajan got 2 anna 13 gonda one kara and one Kranti measuring an area of 28 decimal of land; that Mayajan died, leaving one daughter Delbaru Bibi and brother Meseruddin; that Meseruddin got 70 decimals ofland by inheritance; and that Meseruddin died leaving 3 sons Abdul Hamid, Abdul Latif, Abdul Gani and that later on Abdul Hamid died, leaving plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 and Abdul Latif died, leaving plaintiff Nos. 3 to 5 as heirs. 

 4. It is also contended that the plaintiff got two-third share of Meseruddin measuring an area of 46.50 decimals of land and Abdul Gani got the rest one-third share of Meseruddin measuring an area of 23.25 decimals of land and the rest of the land belonged to defendant Nos. 1 to 9; that the land of CS plot Nos. 201 and 202 corresponding to RS plots Nos. 545 and 546 comprising an area of 1.98 acres which was included in RS khatian Nos. 168, 169, 172.; that RS khatian No. 172 bearing RS plot No. 546 comprising 1.10 acres corresponding SA khatian No. 225 was wrongly recorded in the name of predecessors of defendant Nos. 19 to 22; that RS and SA khatian was also wrongly prepared, and that the plaintiffs have been possessing in ejmali with the co-sharers. 

 5. It is further stated that the suit property was never sold in auction; that Rupsha Fakir did not auction purchase the land of CS 30 khatian; that 'Kha' schedule disputed order of review case No.2 of 1994 is illegal, without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiffs; and that the co-sharer defendants refused to accept an amicable partition on 9-11-1994 and hence the instant suit was filed by the plaintiffs. 

 6. The defendant Nos. 19, 20 and 21 filed joint written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable; that the plaintiffs have no cause of action; that the suit is barred by limitation; that the plaintiffs have no right, title and possession in the suit property, and that the plaintiffs have no locus standi or legal character to challenge the 'Kha' schedule disputed order. The further case of the contesting defendants is that at Mouja Chadkati, the land of CS khatian 30 belonged to Alif Khalifa and others and, superior landlords were Sattajit Ghosal Bahadur and others and the rent of the superior landlord remained unpaid, and the superior landlord filed rent suit No. 1110 of 1911 in the Court of Second Munsif, Barisal, and the said rent suit was decreed and the superior landlord filed Rent Execution Case No. 1192 of 1991 in the Second Court of Munsif Barisal and the land of CS khatian No. 30 being a total area of 2.15 acres was put to auction; that Rupsha Fakir auction purchased the land of CS Khatian No. 30 on 23-4-1915; that the sale was confirmed on 30-8-1915 and that the said auction purchaser got sale certificate and also got the delivery of possession through Court. 

 7. It is further stated that lmanullah and Amina Khatoon took 9 years "Meyadi Kolkarsha pattan" from the auction purchaser Rupsha Fakir measuring an area of 69 decimals of land by executing and registering a Kabuliat dated First Srabon, 1326 BS and paid rent to Rupsha Fakir by holding over after the expiry of the term of alleged Kabuliyat; that later Rupsha Fakir transferred 91.50 decimals of land in favour of defendant No. 19, Abdul Sabur Howlader by a kabala dated 10 Srabon, 1344 BS corresponding to 23-7-1937 from CS khatian No. 30 bearing CS plot Nos. 201 and 202; that he amicably got possession from CS plot No. 202 and defendant No. 19 had been possessing that kabulati land that Imanullah got 69 decimals of land by pattan from auction purchaser Rupsha Fakir; that Imanullah died leaving defendant Nos. 19 to 22 as his heirs and thus defendant Nos. 19 to 22 got 69 decimals  9-1/2 decimals totaling 1.60-1/2 aores of land and had been possessing the same with the other co-sharers and also paid rents. 

 8. It is further contented that Hinguludin, the predecessor of defendant Nos. 1 to 7, also purchased some land from auction purchaser Rupsha Fakir, by a kabala dated 20-3-1920; and that Meseruddin Munshi, the predecessor of the plaintiff also purchased 41 decimals of hind from CS 'khatian No. 30 corresponding to CS plot No. 201 with other land from the auction purchaser Rupsha Fakir, by a kabala No. 1404 of 1920 dated 7th Chaitra, 1326 BS corresponding to 8-4-1920. 

 10. It is also stated that the divisible land of SA Khatian No. 225.bearing plot No. 546 was acquired by the government vide LA case No. 49 of 196162 and defendant No. 19 Sabur Mia, released that land vide Miscellaneous case No. 29 of 1986 from the alleged LA case and defendant No. 19 deposited the government dues and that present RS and SA khatians were correctly prepared; that the alleged auction purchase is legal and acted upon and the disputed order of Kha schedule is legal and fair; that the claim and cause of action of the plaintiffs is false, and that solenama filed by the plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 1-3, 8,9, 11 to 13 was collusive and fraudulent arid as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 13. On behalf of the defendant Nos. 19 and 20 Exhibits A, A1, B, B1, C, D, E, F, F1 and G (1 to 9) have been filed in support of their contention. Exhibit A is Kabliyat of first Srobhan, 1326 BS, Exhibit A1 is Kabala No. 2638 dated 23-7-1937, Exhibits Band Blare the certified copy of the order sheet and solenama in review Miscellaneous case No.2 of 1994, Exhibit C is the certified copy of the RS khatian No. 172, Exhibits D and D 1 are certified copies of SA khatian respectively. Exhibit E is the certified copy of the order sheet in Miscellaneous Case No. 29 of 1986-87, Exhibit F is the treasury challan, Exhibit F 1 is the latter regarding release order from acquisition and Exhibits G (1 to 9) are the Dhakalas given by the superior landlord. 

 17. Mr Abdul Quyaum along with Mr Shamsuddin Howlader on behalf of the petitioners, submits that the learned Appellate Court ought to have believed that the land of CS khatian No. 30 put to auction vide Rent Suit No. 1110 of 1911 in the Court of Munsif, 2nd Court, Barisal, and Rent Execution Case No. 1192 of 1911 was started out of the decree and ultimately, the land was auction purchased by Rupsha Fakir on 20-4-1915 and the auction sale was confirmed and Rupsha Fakir got the sale certificate who was also issued delivery of possession through Court. He further submits that thereafter Rupsha Fakir leased out 69 decimals of land in favour of the predecessor of defendant Nos. 19 to 22 Imanullah and Amena Khatoon on the first Shroban, 1326 BS by way of Kubliyat; that Rupsha Fakir also sold some land in favour of Hinguluddin on 20-3-1920 who is the predecessor of defendant Nos. 1 to 7; that Rupsha Fakir also sold some portion of land to Meser Ali, the predecessor of the plaintiffs, on 8-4-1920 vide kabala deed No. 1404, and that Rupsha Fakir transferred 91.50 decimals of land to defendant No. 19 by a kabala dated 23-7-1937 and the facts of auction purchase was written in the body of the said kabala deed. It is further submitted that the learned trial Court legally and rightly considered the Exhibits Nos. A and A 1 and made an observation that the land of CS khatian No. 30 was put to auction for the arrear of rent and Rupsha Fakir auction purchased the said land and the auction sale was acted upon, but the learned lower appellate Court misconceived and misunderstood that fact and came to an erroneous decision without considering the evidence of PW and DWs and the documents filed by the contesting defendants and thus he reversed the judgment and decree of the trial Court whimsically which is liable to be set aside. 

 27. On the other hand, the contesting defendants examined 2 DWs, DW 1 Abdul Sabur Howlader is defendant No. 12 and DW 2 Chan Fakir is a contiguous land holder. DW 1 deposed in support of the contention of the contesting defendants and DW 2 deposed corroborating the evidence of DW 1. Furthermore, the contesting defendant Nos. 19 and 22 have submitted the certified copy of the order sheet dated 23-12-1986 in Miscellaneous Case No. 29 of 1986 marked Exhibit E, the certified copy of the order sheet and solenama in review Miscellaneous Case No.2 of 1994 marked Exhibits B and B 1; and the certified copy of RS khatian No. 172 Exhibit C and SA khatian No. 225 and 183 Exhibits D and D1. All these documents clearly prove the title of Rupsha Fakir by virtue of auction purchase. The kabuliyats dated 1st Shrobon, 1326 BS in favour ofImanuddin by Rupsha Fakir Exhibit A and dakhila Exhibit G (1 to 9) and the kabala dated 23-7-1937 executed by Rupsha Fakir in favour of Abdur Sabur Exhibit A 1 also evidently speaks of the title of the contesting defendants in the suit land. In view of the above facts and evidence on record, we are of the view that the plaintiffs have totally failed to prove their case and their predecessor's title in the suit land has been extinguished by the auction sale of the suit land for arrears of rent and thus the contesting defendants have proved the basis of RS and SA record in respect of the suit land by filing the valid papers of auction sale, Dakhalnama and boynama and the contesting defendants have proved their title by filing and proving the title deeds like kabuliyats, Dhakhilas, kabala and other relevant papers. It is the established principle of law that the party on whom the onus of proof lies must, in order to succeed, establish his case and he cannot, on failure to do so, take advantage of the weakness of his adversary's case. He must succeed by the strength of his own right and the clearness of his own proof. Here in this case the plaintiffs in order to succeed must have to prove their title and possession in the suit land and they can stand on the weakness of the defendants. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record, it is evident that the plaintiffs have totally failed to prove their title and possession in the suit land. Moreover, the case of the contesting defendants is so strong that they cannot even stand on the weakness of their adversary's case. Further- more, it appears from record that defendant Nos. 19, 20 and 22 have made a compromise with the plaintiffs which has no basis and, as such, this compromise appears to be illegal, collusive and fraudulent for which this sort of compromise does not create any title in the suit land.
